data.title: Foreign holdings of US Treasuries rise in August; China holdings drop -data
data.description:
Foreign holdings of U.S. Treasuries edged higher in August after two months of declines, data from the Treasury Department showed on Friday, led by gains in holdings from the UK and Canada.

Holdings of U.S. Treasuries rose to $9.331 trillion in August, from $9.248 trillion in the previous month. Compared with a year earlier, Treasuries owned by foreigners were up less than 1%.

China's holdings, however, dropped to $590.7 billion, the lowest since August 2008

data.title: Delek US Holdings to Host Third Quarter 2026 Conference Call on November 6, 2026
data.description:
Delek US Holdings, Inc. () (“Delek US”) today announced that the Company intends to issue a press release summarizing third quarter 2026 results before the U.S. stock market opens on Friday, November 6, 2026. A conference call to discuss these results is scheduled to begin at 10:00 a.m. CT (11:00 a.m. ET) on Friday, November 6, 2026.

The live broadcast of this conference call will be available online by going to www.DelekUS.com and clicking on the investor relations section of the website. A presentation containing supplemental financial information will also be available online at ir.delekus.com prior to the conference call and webcast. The Company does not intend to furnish this presentation on a Current Report on Form 8-K. Investors are encouraged to review the presentation in conjunction with the Company’s earnings press release and webcast. The online replay will be available on the website for 90 days.

About Delek US Holdings, Inc.

Delek US Holdings, Inc. is a diversified downstream energy company with assets in petroleum refining, logistics, pipelines, and renewable fuels. The refining assets consist primarily of refineries operated in Tyler and Big Spring, Texas, El Dorado, Arkansas and Krotz Springs, Louisiana with a combined nameplate crude throughput capacity of 302,000 barrels per day.

The logistics operations include Delek Logistics Partners, LP (). Delek Logistics Partners, LP is a growth-oriented master limited partnership focused on owning and operating midstream energy infrastructure assets. Delek US Holdings, Inc. and its subsidiaries owned approximately 58.0% (including the general partner interest) of Delek Logistics Partners, LP as of September 30, 2026.

Information about Delek US Holdings, Inc. can be found on its website (www.delekus.com), investor relations webpage (ir.delekus.com), and news webpage (www.delekus.com/news).

data.title: ICE review: Canola Weakens on Seasonal Harvest Pressure
data.description:
WINNIPEG, Manitoba--The ICE Futures canola market was weaker on Friday, hitting fresh seven-week lows as steady farmer selling and bearish technical signals weighed on prices.

  • November canola was down by C$2.90 at C$798.80 per ton, with the move below C$800 per ton bearish from a chart standpoint.
  • Losses in the Chicago soy complex and European rapeseed contributed to the softer tone in canola, although Malaysian palm oil was firmer to end the week.
  • Seasonal harvest pressure remained a bearish influence, as warm and dry forecasts across most of the Prairies this weekend should allow farmers to make good progress bringing in the last of the crop.
  • Farmers delivered 620,100 tons of canola into the commercial pipeline during the week ended Oct. 11, reported the Canadian Grain Commission. While that was down by 19% from the previous week, crop-year-to-date deliveries at 4.45 million tons are 28% ahead of last year's pace.
  • Weekly Canadian canola exports at 158,300 tons were down from 248,400 tons the previous week. Crop-year-to-date exports are up 44% on the year at 1.38 million tons through 10 weeks.
  • There were 113,995 contracts traded on Friday, which compares with Thursday when 107,034 contracts changed hands. Spreading accounted for 81,200 of the contracts traded.

data.title: SoftBank weighs $18 billion acquisition of Allied Universal, Bloomberg News reports
data.description:
SoftBank Group is considering an acquisition of Allied Universal in a deal that could value the US security services provider at about $18 billion, Bloomberg News reported on Friday, citing people familiar with the matter.

  • Allied Universal provides security staffing for businesses, venues and major events, and has a growing presence in the data center industry, supporting both development and operation of facilities

  • The potential acquisition would complement SoftBank founder Masayoshi Son's increasing focus on AI, as he is exploring the use of AI-powered robots across industries, and looking to strengthen the infrastructure needed to support the technology, according to the report

  • With Allied, SoftBank would look to eventually replace some staff with robots to handle security work, the report said, citing one of the people

  • The application of humanoid-like security workers will likely take more time, it reported citing another person

  • Deliberations are preliminary and no final decisions have been made, including on the potential price, the report said

  • SoftBank declined to comment on the report, while Allied Universal did not immediately respond to a Reuters request for comment

  • SoftBank is widely known for making large technology investments through its Vision Fund. It was an early investor in Alibaba, owns a majority stake in Arm, and was a major backer of the office-sharing startup WeWork

  • In October, SoftBank completed the final phase of its planned $30 billion investment in OpenAI, deepening its commitment to the AI company

data.title: Apparel retailer True Religion explores sale, sources say
data.description:
Key points:
  • JPMorgan is running the process, which is at an early stage
  • Company's annual earnings approach $150 million, revenue close to $550 million
  • ACON Investments acquired True Religion in 2024

By Abigail Summerville

Clothing retailer True Religion is exploring options including a full sale or minority stake sale that could value the brand, known for its denim, at close to $1 billion, according to people familiar with the matter.

The company, owned by ACON Investments, is working with JPMorgan on the process, which is at an early stage, the people said, requesting anonymity to discuss a confidential matter.

ACON acquired True Religion almost two years ago, and since then the company's earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, and amortization (EBITDA) have nearly doubled, approaching $150 million annually, the people said. The brand generates close to $550 million of annual revenue, they said.

True Religion, ACON and JPMorgan declined to comment.

Founded in 2002, True Religion launched in Los Angeles as a premium jeans brand popular with celebrities and known for its bold "Super T" stitching. Fifteen years later, it went bankrupt twice, in 2017 and then during the pandemic in 2020, as consumer tastes shifted away from denim and towards athleisure and more affordable brands.

True Religion now offers lower-priced denim and a broader range of products across categories, genders and age groups.

Jeans account for 35% to 40% of its revenue, its CEO Michael Buckley said on a podcast this month. The company describes itself as an "urban casual lifestyle brand" and has benefited from shoppers' nostalgia for early 2000s style.

The El Segundo, California-based company operates around 60 brick-and-mortar stores with a goal to hit 150 stores, Buckley said on the podcast.

ACON acquired a controlling stake in the business in December 2024 alongside SB360 Capital Partners, an affiliate of the Schottenstein family, veterans of the retail industry. Jay Schottenstein, chairman of SB360, serves as CEO of American Eagle Outfitters .

data.title: Treasury Yields Fall in Week as Turmoil Subsides — Market Talk
data.description:
1552 ET - Treasury yields fall this week as bond markets turbulence subsides. Fed officials signal no rush to raise rates, while Chairman Warsh stays away from guidance. Derivatives indicate investors' one-year inflation expectations drift away from the Fed's 2% target and reach 2.64%, the highest since June, according to LSEG. U.S. industrial production increases more than expected in September. Oil rises 3.5%. The 30-year has its largest weekly decline since April 2025, falling 0.162 percentage point to 5.436%. The 10-year falls 0.146 point to 5.097% and is down for two consecutive weeks. The two-year sheds 0.055 point to 4.734%, down for three straight weeks. (paulo.trevisani@wsj.com; @ptrevisani)

1331 ET - Major cryptocurrencies are weaker, with sizably-lower volumes seen in afternoon trading, according to data from Coinglass. Trading volumes for bitcoin over the past 24 hours are off 39%, to $49.2 billion. Other tokens are seeing larger decreases in volume, with ethereum volume off 42% to $34.3 billion, HYPE volume down 41% to $1.8 billion, and XRP falling 42% to $2.1 billion. Outflows in bitcoin futures have picked up in the last 5 minutes, according to Coinglass--with outflows seen at $75.2 million and inflows at $31 million. Bitcoin is down 1% to $81,177, ethereum falls 1.3% to $2,419, and XRP slides 2.8% to $1.30. (kirk.maltais@wsj.com)

1235 ET - Weaker activity will likely give Brazil's central bank room to keep cutting its hefty interest rates, TS Lombard's João Pedro Oliveira Fachetti says in a note. He expects the BCB to shave a quarter of a percentage point on November 4 and another in December, bringing the Selic rate to 13.25% by year end, while "further cuts hinge on the approval of structural reforms." President Lula da Silva faces right-wing challenger Flavio Bolsonaro in the final round of vote on October 25 in a tight race. Bolsonaro is seen as a fiscal hawk and Fachetti says his eventual victory could strengthen the Brazilian real, helping contain inflationary pressures. The real climbs 0.3% against the dollar. (paulo.trevisani@wsj.com; @ptrevisani)

1139 ET - Solana, the crypto token with the fifth-largest market capitalization in the market, excluding stablecoins, is supported by a transaction speed that's exponentially higher than its competitors, says Zach Pandl of Grayscale in a note. Pandl says that solana averages roughly 1,400 transactions per second, well exceeding the next-fastest competitor Binance Coins's 200 transactions per second, and other crypto tokens at speeds of roughly 40 transactions per second. Solana's transaction speed is scheduled to accelerate next week with the introduction of its so-called 'Alpenglow' upgrade, which Pandl says will put the token further ahead as a blockchain for developers to use speed-wise. After trading higher earlier in the day, solana is now down 1.3% to $104.17. (kirk.maltais@wsj.com)

1120 ET - A weaker USD index is giving many major cryptocurrencies support. This week has seen bitcoin and other crypto tokens responding more to macro market moves and less to how tech and AI stocks move, says Colin Basco of Coinbase Institutional in a note. "Bitcoin's correlation with chip stocks has also fallen to well under half its January peak, indicating that the market is no longer treating bitcoin as a leveraged proxy for technology stocks," says Basco. He adds that spot demand for bitcoin and other cryptocurrencies remains the "soft spot" for prices, especially as odds for a rate hike before the end of the month are seen rising. Bitcoin is up 0.1% to $82,106, while ethereum rises 0.4% to $2,460. (kirk.maltais@wsj.com)

1109 ET - A solid rise in U.S. industrial production in September still leaves some lukewarm indicators. Production rises 0.7% in the month. Citi's Veronica Clark and Andrew Hollenhorst say in a note that "manufacturing production has moved mostly sideways since the spring and remains below production levels of 2014-18." They add that manufacturing production rose "a more modest" 0.3%. "While strong AI-demand has boosted business investment, much of this investment is imported, implying domestic production has not been as strong," Clark and Hollenhorst say. They add that higher interest rates and fading fiscal support represent headwinds to non-AI manufacturing into 2027. (paulo.trevisani@wsj.com; @ptrevisani)

1033 ET - Unlike in recent years, the British economy has sustained its early-year momentum into the second half of 2026, Oxford Economics' Andrew Goodwin says in a note. "This likely reflects a combination of genuine strength due to structural change because of IT-related investment, but also noisy data," he says. Rapid increases in AI usage mean recent IT strength will likely endure, though strong pickup in professional services output in the last six months is harder to explain. Any resilience will come under pressure over the next few quarters, particularly given most of the impact of the Middle East war is still to come. Financial conditions have worsened, and fiscal policy is being tightened, he adds. (edward.frankl@wsj.com)

1026 ET - If Albertans and Quebecois did vote to leave Canada, what would that mean for the rest of the country? Capital Economics' Bradley Saunders argues the blow to GDP from losing Quebec industry and Alberta oil and gas could be mediated somewhat by continued free trade, companies relocating from seceding provinces to the rest of Canada and a weaker Canadian dollar boosting export competitiveness in other sectors. As such, the economist expects the rest of Canada to outperform the two provinces, whose newfound independence would likely require fiscal tightening. Of course secession would be a lengthy and complicated process without precedent and as such there remains a lot of uncertainty, Saunders says. (robb.stewart@wsj.com; @RobbMStewart)

1026 ET - Canada's housing market remains soft, with a combination of higher fixed mortgage rates and potential Bank of Canada tightening likely keeping buyers on the defensive, Bank of Montreal's Robert Kavcic says. The economist continues to argue that market pricing of a percentage point in interest rates increases in 2027 is too aggressive, but says the balance of risk is tilting to the upside for variable rates into the coming spring market for housing. "This poses an issue for the market given that variable rates are currently the lowest available by a relatively wide margin, and most buyers have pivoted to that space," he says. (robb.stewart@wsj.com; @RobbMStewart)

1024 ET - Elevated oil prices boosted Canada's purchasing power but the gains are uneven across the country, Royal Bank of Canada says. Real gross domestic income expanded 3.1% on-year in 2Q, nearly triple the pace of real GDP growth after a 46% surge in oil added about C$12 billion a quarter to export revenue. Royal Bank says oil producers and resource-rich provinces are capturing a disproportionate share of the initial windfall, while most households face higher costs without offsetting income gains. This complicates monetary policy, since the Bank of Canada controls only one interest rate for the entire country, Royal Bank adds. (robb.stewart@wsj.com; @RobbMStewart)

1018 ET - The rise in mortgage rates has sent Canada's housing market into reverse, with sales and prices both falling in September, says Capital Economics' Stephen Brown. With the risk mortgage rate rise further prices could fall a bit more in the coming months, though Brown doesn't anticipate the Bank of Canada will lift its policy rate as aggressively as markets are pricing in. Lenders have been forced to pass on higher funding costs to fixed mortgage rates. Yet while home prices may fall near term, Brown says he is more upbeat about the outlook from mid-2027 as mortgage rates drop back next year. (robb.stewart@wsj.com; @RobbMStewart)

1011 ET - The widening of spreads between French and German government bond yields has had as much, or possibly more, negative impact on the euro as widening Treasury-German spreads, Standard Chartered's Steve Englander says in a note. "Rising French credit default swaps (CDS) also have a significant impact on euro; although the relationship is not as tight as with the French-German spread, the CDS correlation still supports the view of concerns about France's government finances." The euro faces renewed depreciation if spreads widen further, he says. The euro rises 0.3% to $1.1256 after hitting a 17-month low of $1.1112 Wednesday, LSEG data show. (renae.dyer@wsj.com)

data.title: Air Canada, United to add routes, increase flight capacity in 2027
data.description:
Air Canada and United Airlines plan to expand their Canada-US networks next summer, adding new routes and increasing flight capacity under a transborder partnership that the carriers have agreed to renew, subject to regulatory approval.

Air Canada will introduce service from Toronto to Louisville on April 28, 2027, followed by flights from Montreal to Indianapolis and Edmonton to Newark beginning June 1. It will also deploy larger Airbus A220 aircraft on its Edmonton-San Francisco route to increase capacity.

United plans seasonal flights between Newark and St. John's, Newfoundland, and new services linking Denver with Ottawa and Quebec City. The carrier will also increase flights between Washington, D.C., and Quebec City and boost daily seats between Denver and Winnipeg by 65%.

The expansion builds on a joint business agreement established in 2022 that has enabled 20 new transborder routes, according to Air Canada . The partnership supports more than 1,200 connecting itineraries between Canada and the United States.

Air Canada said an application seeking approval of the renewed and expanded agreement had been submitted to Transport Canada.

The carriers said the additional services would broaden travel options and improve connections through their respective networks. The announcement comes amid softer cross-border demand in recent months.

data.title: SV Biotech Crossover Opportunities Fund LP Discloses Investment at TRex Bio with 7.0% Stake
data.description:
SV Biotech Crossover Opportunities Fund LP acquired a 7.0% stake in TRex Bio, Inc.'s common stock. The fund bought 957,143 shares in the Oct. 8, 2026 IPO and saw 963,524 preferred shares convert at the Oct. 13 closing. The move positions the London-based life sciences investor as a notable early backer after the listing.

Investor Intent

SV Biotech Crossover Opportunities Fund LP says it invested for long-term value but keeps its options open. The fund may talk with other shareholders and TRex Bio’s leadership and considers “making proposals to TRex Bio concerning changes to the capitalization, ownership structure, board structure, or operations.” It also reserves the right to buy more shares, sell shares, or pursue “short selling or any hedging or similar transaction with respect to the shares.”

A 180-day IPO lock-up limits sales, transfers, and hedging unless the underwriters consent, which keeps the position stable through the lock-up period. After that, the fund and other holders can use registration rights to seek public sales through demand or piggyback offerings, subject to the agreement’s caps and timing rules.

Investor's Background

SV Biotech Crossover Opportunities Fund LP is a United Kingdom private fund limited partnership focused on life sciences investing. It is affiliated with SV Health Investors, a long-running venture firm known for backing biotech and healthcare companies across private and public markets. The crossover strategy targets late-stage private and newly public biotech names with a research-driven, long-term approach.
